message.content:
Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5, branch lazy). Uncommitted changes: run
"git diff" there. New feature: option arith-liastar-main-solver moves the lazy LIA* cell
enumeration from a per-lambda subsolver into the MAIN solver. Design (see MainEnum in
src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h and mainSolverCheckStar/advanceStage/
emitDriverLemma/getModelDisjunct/getMainEnum/addEnumLemma in liastar_extension.cpp):
- lambda bound vars -> fresh integer skolems y; base(y) = predicate (ites/nots removed) + y>=0.
- Stage guards: h_0 => base(y); per discovered cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with
  h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k(y)); en.guard is the current h_k; each h is
  ensureLiteral'd and preferPhase'd true. h_0 additionally gets a split lemma.
- Driver lemma per (literal, stage): literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k), unguarded,
  where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal] (under-approximation built by processDisjunct)
  and p[v] is the vector predicate. Claimed satisfiability-preserving.
- Each full-effort round: catch up stages for cones discovered via other literals; if
  guard fixed false at level 0 (Valuation::isFixed) -> emit exact equivalence
  (processDisjunct complete=true); if guard true in SAT assignment -> read the cell from
  arithModel via getModelDisjunct (substitute+rewrite each atom of base; equality atoms
  false in model become strict inequalities; skolems missing from arithModel fall back to
  TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue), dedupe against d_lazyCones, advanceStage, then
  processDisjunct(false) emits the guarded equivalence g_k => (literal = star_k) and
  deactivates the previous g; then emitDriverLemma for the new stage.
- Tests: all 9 regress1/arith/liastar tests pass in this mode (Debug), and in the other
  three modes (accumulate/push-pop/eager); unit test passes.
Focus ONLY on problems introduced by the new main-solver mode (not pre-existing issues in
the subsolver paths). Report findings with concrete code references.
Lens: cvc5 mechanics. Questions to attack:
1. ensureLiteral + preferPhase during a full-effort check: legal at that point? (compare the
   existing liastarGuard pattern). Any issue calling them per stage (many stages)?
2. addEnumLemma skips lemmas that rewrite to constants -- could skipping h_k => not(D_k) (if it
   ever rewrites to true) silently break the stage invariant?
3. getModelDisjunct's use of arithModel keys: substitution with non-leaf keys (the arith model
   map can contain non-variable terms); is substitute() over atom nodes safe/correct here?
4. TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue fallback: legal for skolems unknown to the linear solver?
5. Lemma flushing: every path in mainSolverCheckStar ends in doPendingLemmas or processDisjunct
   (which calls it) -- verify, including the early-return paths in checkFullEffort around the
   model-value shortcut.
6. The unused 'seeded' warning, unused includes, style of the new code vs file conventions.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

findings.title: Driver lemma is not satisfiability-preserving: missing/stale star branch causes wrong unsat (confirmed)
findings.detail: emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1008-1036) emits the unguarded lemma `literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k)` where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal]. Two holes: (1) On the first emission for a literal, d_lastStarLia has no entry, so the star branch is OMITTED entirely (liastar_extension.cpp:1028-1032). The under-approximation always contains the zero vector (empty sum), so the emitted clause `literal => (p[v] or h_0)` wrongly excludes the model v = 0 when p[v] is false and base is unsatisfiable (h_0 fixed false). CONFIRMED: `(assert (<= v 0)) (assert (int.star-contains (lambda ((x Int)) (and (<= x 0) (>= x 1))) v))` is sat (v=0 is the empty sum) but `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers unsat (/tmp/liastar_zero3.smt2; eager and subsolver modes instead hit a pre-existing 1-D `mkNode(AND, single-element)` arity crash at liastar_extension.cpp:1202/449, so the wrong answer is specific to the new driver lemma). (2) The catch-up loop (liastar_extension.cpp:1060-1070) advances stages for cones discovered through another literal sharing the lambda, but never updates d_lastStarLia[literal]; emitDriverLemma at lines 1077/1102 then pairs the NEW stage guard with a STALE star (built over fewer cones). When that stage guard later becomes fixed false (enumeration complete), the clause forces `p[v] or star_stale`, which is strictly stronger than the exact equivalence and can prune real models, again producing wrong unsat. Fix direction: emitDriverLemma should always include a current under-approximation (e.g. recompute via getStarConstraints(literal), which is exact for zero cones: v = 0), and the catch-up path must refresh it before pairing it with a new guard. The doc comment claiming the lemma is satisfiability preserving (liastar_extension.cpp:1017-1020, liastar_extension.h driver description) is wrong as implemented.

findings.title: MainEnum state outlives user-context-scoped lemmas: wrong sat after pop in incremental mode (confirmed)
findings.detail: All guard-chain lemmas (h_0 => base, h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k), drivers) are sent as ordinary theory lemmas and are RETRACTED on user-context pop, but the bookkeeping that gates their emission lives in non-context-dependent std::maps: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:450-462), plus en.negated and en.guard inside MainEnum. getMainEnum only seeds h_0 => base once per lambda lifetime (liastar_extension.cpp:823-884), advanceStage lemmas are emitted once per cone (en.negated never resets), and emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard. After a pop, en.guard refers to a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it: the SAT solver can set it true while the skolems sit in an already-covered cell; mainSolverCheckStar then re-harvests a known cell, the dedupe path (liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) re-emits an already-cached driver, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, and the candidate model is accepted. CONFIRMED: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (check (1 1) unsat, pop, then check (2 1) with the same lambda, which is also unsat since 2+1 < 5) answers `unsat` then `sat` in main-solver mode; subsolver mode answers `unsat`/`unsat`. The subsolver mode is immune because its accumulated state lives in the subsolver, not in the main SAT solver's retractable clause database. Note the existing regress test simple.smt2 uses push/pop but masks this because its second query is certified via the p[v] split. Fix direction: make the per-lambda/per-literal gating user-context-dependent (CDO/CDHashMap on userContext()), or re-seed the full chain when the user context changes.

findings.title: No-progress rounds silently accept the candidate model without certifying the star literal
findings.detail: Every failure path in mainSolverCheckStar 're-emits' the driver and returns: guard unassigned or false-but-not-fixed (liastar_extension.cpp:1095-1105), getModelDisjunct returning null (1111-1117), and the dedupe hit (1118-1128). But the driver for the current stage was already emitted when the stage was opened (d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard always holds by then), so emitDriverLemma is a no-op and doPendingLemmas flushes nothing. TheoryArith::postCheck (src/theory/arith/theory_arith.cpp:292-298) then proceeds with no lemma sent and the candidate model is accepted -- there is no 'next round' to 'try again' in, and the extension never calls d_im.setModelUnsound. This is sound only when the SAT assignment certifies the literal via the p[v] or star branches of the driver clause; it is NOT sound when (a) the guard branch is the satisfied one but the harvest failed (null disjunct: skolem missing from arithModel with null/non-const candidate value, atoms not evaluating to constants), or (b) the literal is asserted NEGATIVELY (the driver is vacuous for not(literal), and nothing certifies v not-in S* until the exact equivalence is emitted; if the guard is false at a non-zero decision level the round emits nothing). Path (a)+dedupe is exactly the mechanism behind the confirmed wrong-sat in the push/pop counterexample. By contrast, the subsolver mode (lazyCheckStar/lazyHilbert) makes progress every round: the subsolver always yields either a new cell or completeness, so a refinement lemma is always sent until the literal is fully reduced. Fix direction: when a round makes no progress for an unreduced literal, either force progress (e.g. split on the skolem atoms / re-assert the chain) or mark the model unsound so sat is not answered.

findings.title: Cell dedupe compares raw harvested disjunct against the normalized stored node, so it misses semantically equal cells
findings.detail: mainSolverCheckStar's re-harvest guard (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) compares `pair.first == disjunct` where `disjunct` is the raw output of getModelDisjunct (which produces `atom.notNode()` literals for atoms false in the model, liastar_extension.cpp:964-968), while `pair.first` stored in d_lazyCones is the output of `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix(variables, removeItesAndNots(disjunct)).second` (processDisjunct, liastar_extension.cpp:1183-1197; getMatrix returns its input node, liastar_utils.cpp:883-941). Whenever the harvested cell contains at least one negated atom, the raw and stored forms differ syntactically and the dedupe never fires; the same cell is then run through processDisjunct again, appending a duplicate cone and duplicate star skolems/constraints (semantically harmless but bloats the encoding, and the protection the comment claims does not exist). Compare the normalized form instead (apply removeItesAndNots before the comparison), or store the raw form alongside the cone.

findings.title: getCandidateModelValue fallback can produce an ill-formed integer constant (debug assertion failure)
findings.detail: getModelDisjunct's fallback (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:915-927) calls TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue for skolems missing from arithModel. The liastar extension runs BEFORE sanityCheckIntegerModel (theory_arith.cpp:287-325), and collectModelValues filters integer variables with fractional simplex values into d_arithModelCacheIllTyped rather than arithModel -- i.e. the skolem is missing from arithModel precisely in the rare case its candidate value is non-integral. The fallback then reaches TheoryArithPrivate::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith_private.cpp:1080-1097), which does mkConstRealOrInt(term.getType(), qmodel); for an Int-typed skolem with non-integral qmodel this calls mkConstInt, whose Assert(r.isIntegral()) (node_manager_template.cpp:1446-1449) aborts debug builds, and in production builds yields a CONST_INTEGER node wrapping a non-integral rational that passes the value.isConst() check and corrupts the harvested cell. For skolems entirely unknown to the simplex the path is safe (getDeltaValue throws ModelException, caught, returns null, handled at liastar_extension.cpp:920-923). Guard the fallback with a type/integrality check (e.g. reject values whose type does not match the skolem). Also note getDeltaValue's AlwaysAssert(d_qflraStatus != Result::UNKNOWN) is satisfied in this calling context (linear postCheck completed without conflict).

findings.title: Mechanics review: ensureLiteral/preferPhase legal, addEnumLemma skip safe, lemma flushing verified, no compiler warnings
findings.detail: Answers to the remaining review questions, all verified against the code: (Q1) ensureLiteral+preferPhase during full-effort check mirrors the pre-existing liastarGuard pattern (processDisjunct, liastar_extension.cpp:1249-1251); PropEngine::ensureLiteral on a fresh boolean skolem only registers a CNF literal (prop_engine.cpp:603-618) and TheoryInferenceManager::preferPhase re-calls ensureLiteral internally (theory_inference_manager.cpp:564-568, harmlessly redundant).
